The metronome

A loop keeps time in the graph. Drive five firings, then open any triggered_by edge: the fan itself is the run history.

Live graph behavior 5 beats · 5 edges · 0 log tables
Solid ink — shipped and true today Ghost ink — designed, not built

01Make the history

Each click is one scheduled firing. It creates a real work-session node and one inbound triggered_by edge to the loop. The sequence runs once and settles.

The loop is waiting. Its inbound edge fan is empty.

Select a visible triggered_by edge to open that firing’s work.
  1. Beat 1 creates the Aug 15 Dreamer work session and an inbound triggered_by edge to the loop.
  2. Beat 2 creates the Aug 16 Dreamer work session and another inbound edge.
  3. Beat 3 creates the Aug 17 Dreamer work session and another inbound edge.
  4. Beat 4 creates the Aug 18 Dreamer work session and another inbound edge.
  5. Beat 5 creates the Aug 19 Dreamer work session. The five inbound edges are the run history.

No separate log is hiding behind the picture. A graph read of the loop’s inbound triggered_by edges returns this history.

02The loop’s real anatomy

A loop is one entity with three pieces: when to fire, what to spawn, and what instruction the spawned work receives. These fields mirror the shipped Dreamer loop.

schedule≤ 200 chars
"every 1d"
spawn configuration
{
  "teamMemberId": "01a0…fff6",
  "subjectId": null,
  "config": {}
}
prompt≤ 20,000 chars
Daily memory sweep. Walk this space's teammates and the memories they remember, mark what is stale or contradicted, and consolidate overlapping clusters. Report what you changed on this task.

The shipped example is Dreamer daily sweep: enabled, scheduled every 1d, assigned to Dreamer, with no subject pin and an empty configuration object.

03The edge is the receipt

Registered today

triggered_by runs from a task or work_session to a loop. Its optional firedAt property records the firing time.

That direction matters: the loop’s inbound edges answer “what did this schedule launch?” Each source opens the real work entity.

Steering

  • Edit the loop’s content to change its schedule, spawn settings, or prompt.
  • Message the loop because every entity is an anchor.
  • Soft-delete it to stop future firings.

All mutations remain permission- and version-guarded.

04The neighboring truths

Loops sit beside memory and spells in Advanced Help. Keep their boundaries sharp.

memory · solid ink

Memories are first-class, append-only graph entities. Any entity can remembers a memory. Borrowed --memory injection writes nothing; the persona working set arrives before task memories.

Dispatcher selects and attaches memory at spawn time. Dreamer gardens it asynchronously, away from a working agent’s critical path.

spell runtime · ghost ink

The spell kind and equips/pulled graph plumbing exist. Spell casting and hooks do not.

Not built yetNo page should animate a spell being cast or a hook firing as if that runtime ships today.
